title: Make a passport or ID photo at home on your iPhone (no photo booth)
body:
You don't need a photo booth for a passport or visa photo. On an iPhone you can shoot a compliant one at home in under a minute — if the app handles the three hard parts: the exact size for your country, a clean white background, and the right head position.

**What a compliant photo needs**
- The correct size (US 2×2 in / 51×51 mm; most countries 35×45 mm; Canada 50×70 mm).
- A plain, even background (usually white).
- Head height and eye line within range.

I built **[Snapport](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6780575828)** for exactly this: country size templates, automatic background replacement, head-position guides, and a print-ready sheet — processed on-device, one-time purchase, no subscription.

Reference: free passport-size table by country → https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/data/passport-photo-sizes.html

title: Free printable Zhuyin (Bopomofo) practice sheets for teaching kids Chinese
body:
If you're teaching a child Zhuyin (Bopomofo, ㄅㄆㄇ) — the phonetic system used in Taiwan — repeated writing practice is what makes the 37 symbols stick.

I made a few **free, printable web tools** (no signup) for parents and teachers:
- Practice sheets (田字格 tracing) → https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/zhuyin-practice-sheet.html
- Flashcards → https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/zhuyin-flashcards.html
- Bingo cards for the classroom → https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/zhuyin-bingo.html
- Symbol chart → https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/zhuyin-bopomofo-chart.html

To learn the symbols through play, **[Lumi Bopomofo](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6773017109)** turns all 37 into games — free to download with a one-time lifetime unlock, no ads, no subscription, everything on-device.

title: Scan documents to searchable PDFs offline — one-time purchase, no cloud
body:
Most scanner apps push a subscription and upload your documents to their cloud. For sensitive papers (IDs, contracts, receipts) that's the opposite of what you want.

**What to look for in a scanner app**
- OCR so scans become *searchable* PDFs.
- Everything on-device — no upload, no account.
- A lock (Face ID) for private documents.
- Offline, and a one-time price.

I built **[ScanTo Pro](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6779977651)** to do exactly that: scan → OCR → searchable PDF → Face ID lock, fully offline, pay once.

If you're comparing pay-once vs subscription tools generally, I keep a 5-year cost breakdown here → https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/subscription-swap.html

title: Track spending in hours of your life, not dollars
body:
A $60 gadget isn't really "$60" — it's however long *you* had to work to earn it after tax. Framing purchases in **hours of your life** makes impulse spending feel very different.

**How to think about it**
1. Work out your real hourly take-home (after tax and work costs).
2. Divide a price by that number.
3. Ask: is this worth *that many hours*?

I built **[HoursTag](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6754218117)** to do this automatically: set your hourly value once, and every price shows up as hours. It's a one-time purchase, no subscription, and nothing leaves your device.

It's a surprisingly calming way to spend less without a strict budget.

title: Get your résumé past the ATS filter (a quick checklist)
body:
Most résumés are first read by software (an ATS), not a human. If the parser can't read yours, a person never sees it.

**Quick ATS checklist**
- Use a simple, single-column layout — no text boxes or images for key info.
- Match keywords from the job description (skills, tools, titles).
- Standard section headings (Experience, Education, Skills).
- Save as PDF unless the posting says otherwise.
- Quantify results ( "cut build time 40%" beats "improved builds").

I built **[CV Desk](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6781337213)** to score your résumé against ATS rules instantly and give recruiter-ready templates — one-time purchase, no subscription. Résumé conventions also differ by country (photo or not, length, personal details): free reference → https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/data/resume-cv-conventions-by-country.html

title: Free up iPhone storage: find duplicate photos and huge videos
body:
"Storage Almost Full" is almost always duplicates, near-identical burst shots, and a few enormous videos — not your actual memories.

**A fast cleanup pass**
1. Find exact + near-duplicate photos and keep the best one.
2. Sort videos by size; the biggest few usually free the most space.
3. Clear old screenshots and blurry shots.

I built **[PicClear](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6780223070)** to do this in one scan — similar-shot grouping, largest-videos view — all on-device, one-time purchase, no subscription.

No cloud upload, no account: it just cleans up locally.

title: A period tracker that stays on your device (no account, no data selling)
body:
Cycle-tracking apps are some of the most privacy-sensitive apps on your phone — yet many upload your data and monetize it. For something this personal, on-device is the only sane default.

**What to look for**
- Data stored on-device, not in someone's cloud.
- No account / no sign-up required.
- A clear view of phases, fertile window, and gentle days.
- A one-time price, not a subscription on your own health data.

I built **[Cyca](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6782251621)** to do exactly that: private period & cycle tracking that stays on your iPhone — pay once, no account, nothing uploaded.

title: Sharpen a blurry photo on iPhone without uploading it anywhere
body:
Most "AI photo enhancer" apps send your photo to a server. For personal photos — kids, family, documents — that's a lot of trust for a blur fix.

**On-device enhancement, in short**
- Super-resolution reconstructs detail and upscales.
- Doing it locally means the photo never leaves your phone.
- No subscription needed for occasional fixes.

I built **[Unblurry](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6782275018)** to sharpen and upscale photos entirely **on-device** — pay once, no account, nothing uploaded. Great for old scans, screenshots, and slightly-soft shots.

title: White noise & sleep sounds that actually work offline (no subscription)
body:
White, brown and rain noise genuinely help many people sleep or focus — but sound apps are one of the most aggressively monetized categories, often gating the good sounds or the sleep timer behind a subscription.

**What a good sound app needs**
- A rich library you can *mix* (rain over brown noise, etc.).
- A reliable sleep timer with fade-out.
- Offline playback (no streaming, no data use overnight).
- A one-time price for something you use nightly.

I built **[Sereno](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6788236641)** as a pay-once sound machine: mixable sounds, timers, fully offline — no ads, no subscription.

title: Reclaim focus for deep work: block distracting apps on iOS
body:
Context-switching is the silent tax on deep work. Every glance at a feed costs far more than the seconds it takes — research on interrupted work suggests it can take over 20 minutes to fully refocus.

**A simple focus-block routine**
- Pick one recurring high-risk window: your first work session, right after lunch, or evenings.
- Block only the apps that actually break your focus — not everything.
- Replace the habit with a prepared task: the next failing test, a design doc, a workout.
- Review the hours you got back at the end of each week.

Apple's Screen Time is easy to tap past. When you want an intentional, harder-to-skip block for deep work, I built **[LockHour Pro](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6780107485)** — scheduled focus sessions, one-time purchase, no subscription, on-device.

Curious what one hour a day actually costs over a year? Free calculator → https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/screen-time-calculator.html

title: On-device speech-to-text on iPhone — private, offline, no subscription
body:
Most transcription apps send your audio to a server and charge monthly. For a doctor's visit, a private interview, or a lecture you recorded, that's a lot of trust to hand over for a recurring fee.

**What to look for in a transcription tool**
- Transcription that runs *on your device*, so audio and text never leave the phone.
- Works offline — no account, no upload, no waiting on a server.
- You own the notes: plain-text or Markdown export, not locked in a cloud.
- A one-time price instead of a subscription for something you use a few times a month.

The trade-off is honest: on-device models can be a little less accurate than the biggest cloud engines, and very long recordings take processing time. For most meetings, lectures and voice memos that's a fair price for privacy.

I built **[Sono Note](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6782139553)** around this: record or import audio, transcribe on-device, edit, and export — offline, pay once, no subscription.

If you're weighing pay-once vs subscription tools in general, the 5-year math is usually not close.

title: Drill TOEIC Part 5 and Part 7 offline — without another subscription
body:
If you're grinding toward a higher TOEIC score, most of the gain comes from *reps*: lots of Part 5 grammar/vocab and Part 7 reading under light time pressure, plus focused Part 3 listening.

**What actually helps between now and test day**
- Short, frequent drills you can do on a commute — offline, no login.
- Part-by-part practice (5, 7, 3) so you target your weakest section.
- Pacing practice for Part 7, where slow readers lose easy points.
- Tracking so you see which question types you keep missing.

No app *guarantees* 990 — that comes from consistent practice and real listening/reading. But a tool that removes friction with offline practice and a clear study plan makes daily reps more likely.

I built **[Aim990](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6784974530)** for exactly that: offline TOEIC-style drills by part, with weak-point tracking and a one-time unlock option.

title: Track travel spending in multiple currencies, fully offline
body:
Abroad with cash in a currency you don't think in, budget apps that need a bank login and a signal are exactly the wrong tool. You just want to jot what you spent and see it in your home currency.

**What to look for in a travel spending tracker**
- Manual, cash-friendly entry — no bank connection required.
- Multi-currency with a converter to your home currency as you go.
- Fully offline, so it works on a plane or with no roaming.
- Export (CSV) so you can settle up or expense it later.
- One-time price, not a subscription for a two-week trip.

Rates move, so treat any converted total as an estimate and confirm big numbers with your bank.

I made **[G+Money](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6755782939)** for this: quick multi-currency entries, offline conversion, CSV export, pay once, no account.

title: 11 tiny, free reference datasets (JSON, CC BY 4.0): Bopomofo/IPA, paper & photo sizes, and more
body:
When you build indie apps you keep needing the same small reference tables: the 37 Bopomofo symbols, standard paper sizes, passport-photo dimensions per country, Mandarin tone contours... I kept rebuilding these, so I cleaned them up and open-sourced 11 of them as plain JSON under CC BY 4.0.

**Repo:** https://github.com/alice51849/open-reference-datasets

Each dataset is a single JSON file with descriptive metadata plus the data array, and is also published as a web page with `schema.org/Dataset` markup so search engines and AI tools can pick it up.

**A few that might save you time**

- **Zhuyin (Bopomofo) — 37 symbols**: every symbol with its Hanyu Pinyin, **IPA** transcription, Unicode code point and an example word. Handy for anything that touches Mandarin pronunciation.
- **Mandarin tones**: the four tones + neutral, each with its Chao pitch-contour number and Zhuyin/Pinyin marks.
- **Passport / ID photo sizes by country**: width x height in mm, required head height and background colour.
- **Paper sizes**: ISO A-series and US sizes in mm, inches and pixels.
- **Image file formats** and **common image/video resolutions**: quick lookup tables.
- **TOEIC to CEFR**: score bands mapped to CEFR levels with can-do summaries.
- Plus currency formatting by country, resume/CV conventions by country, and menstrual cycle phases.

**Why plain JSON + a web page?**
The JSON is easy to drop into a project; the HTML version carries `schema.org/Dataset` metadata (name, license, distribution) so it's citable and discoverable. Everything is CC BY 4.0 — use it, adapt it, just keep attribution.

These came out of building a set of small, pay-once, privacy-first iOS apps (a Bopomofo learning game, a passport-photo maker, a document scanner, and so on), where getting these reference values exactly right actually mattered. Figured they might be useful to someone else too.

If you spot an error or want to add a country/row, issues and PRs are welcome.

title: Why Zhuyin still matters after a child can already speak Mandarin
body:
A heritage-language child can speak Mandarin with grandparents and still freeze when they meet an unfamiliar Traditional Chinese character. Speaking and decoding print are different skills.

Zhuyin (Bopomofo) closes that gap. Its 37 symbols and tone marks turn a written character into a pronunciation the child may already understand. Taiwan's official **Ministry of Education Mini Dictionary** uses standard Zhuyin with dictionary entries, so the system is not just a short first-grade unit — it remains a practical bridge for checking pronunciation and reading more independently.

Official reference: https://dict.mini.moe.edu.tw/

**A useful learning sequence**
1. Hear and recognize each symbol before worrying about speed.
2. Add tones, because the same syllable can change meaning.
3. Blend symbols into syllables.
4. Use Zhuyin-annotated stories and dictionary entries in real reading.

I wrote a fuller parent-friendly explanation here: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/answers/why-should-my-child-learn-zhuyin-if-they-already-speak-chinese.html

For playful practice, **[Lumi Bopomofo](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6773017109)** covers all 37 symbols, tones, tracing and blending. It is free to download with a one-time lifetime unlock, has no ads or recurring subscription, and keeps children's progress on-device.

title: A free, print-ready 5-day Zhuyin lesson plan for heritage Chinese schools
body:
Teachers in weekend Chinese schools often have excellent long-form materials but still need a small unit they can print and teach next Saturday. So I made a **free five-day Zhuyin (Bopomofo) starter lesson plan** for ages 4–8.

Lesson plan: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/guides/zhuyin-5-day-lesson-plan-heritage-school.html
Traditional Chinese version: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/zh-Hant/guides/zhuyin-5-day-lesson-plan-heritage-school.html

**What is included**
- Five 30-minute lessons with objectives, timed activities and exit checks.
- A realistic 12-symbol starter set — not an “all 37 symbols in five days” promise.
- Sound-symbol recognition, first blends and tone awareness.
- Adaptations for children who already speak Mandarin, children who rarely hear it, and mixed-level classes.
- Direct references to Taiwan's Ministry of Education Bopomofo handbook and practice book, plus Overseas Community Affairs Council materials.

The plan works with cards, paper, teacher modeling and games; no app is required. Lumi Bopomofo is mentioned only as an optional practice layer between classes.

The original lesson is licensed **CC BY 4.0**, so teachers may print, translate, rearrange and share it with attribution. I also added `schema.org/LearningResource` and FAQ structured data so libraries, search engines and AI tools can identify it as a reusable lesson plan rather than another app landing page.

title: I built a private, no-score 3-minute Zhuyin observation guide
body:
A single “Zhuyin score” is not useful to a family. A child may recognize symbols but not blend them, hear tones but avoid writing, or decode syllables without using them in a real phrase. Combining those interactions into one number would hide the difference.

I built a **free, parent-guided 3-minute Zhuyin (Bopomofo) observation guide** that keeps five choices separate:

1. Symbol recognition
2. Tone awareness
3. Sound blending
4. Shape and writing
5. Reading application

English: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/zhuyin-readiness-check.html
繁體中文: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/zh-Hant/tools/zhuyin-readiness-check.html

The page calculates no total, score, stage, level or ranking. It simply repeats the five observations in words, then shows the same fixed list of free activities—flashcards, a symbol-and-tone chart, a 14-day calendar, a printable tracing sheet and a five-day lesson plan. The family can choose any one activity or stop without assigning a next step.

The implementation is plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript. There is no account, form submission, analytics field, server scoring, local storage or saved child profile. Choices remain only in the current tab and disappear when it is closed or reset. Both language pages have reciprocal `hreflang`, `WebApplication`, `LearningResource`, FAQ and breadcrumb structured data.

Five tiny observations cannot measure all 37 symbols, spoken Mandarin, comprehension, a reading level, school readiness, speech or development. The page states those limits directly rather than pretending a three-minute web tool can assess or label a child.

title: Designing a learning video call without turning family time into a test
body:
A long-distance grandparent can be a wonderful heritage-language partner, but “Can you say this? What sound is that?” quickly turns a family call into a quiz.

I wanted a different design for children learning Zhuyin (Bopomofo): keep the relationship first, make every turn concrete, and let pointing or showing an object count as participation.

The result is a **free bilingual 10-minute grandparent video-call kit**:

- English: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/zhuyin-grandparent-video-call-kit.html
- 繁體中文: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/zh-Hant/tools/zhuyin-grandparent-video-call-kit.html

Each call uses three rotating family words, a camera treasure hunt, one tone gesture and a real family sentence. A nearby parent stabilizes the device and helps both sides attend to the same object. The grandparent models once, waits, and recasts a different pronunciation naturally instead of grading it.

**Being precise about evidence matters.** A longitudinal study of 48 families found that grandparent sensitivity predicted infants’ positive affect during video and in-person interactions. The paper also summarizes evidence for live social contingency and nearby-adult scaffolding during video chat: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9539353/

But that study involved infants, mostly highly educated White/Caucasian families during COVID-19. It did not test Zhuyin, language scores or this activity. The page says that explicitly. The research informed the interaction pattern; it does not justify a “learn faster” claim.

The implementation is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript. It has no account, camera, microphone, form submission, local storage or saved child profile. Both language pages include reciprocal `hreflang`, `LearningResource`, `WebApplication`, FAQ and breadcrumb structured data. The printable routine is CC BY 4.0 so families, libraries and heritage schools can adapt it.

For families who want structured practice between calls, Lumi Bopomofo is an optional layer for all 37 symbols, tones, tracing and blending—not a requirement for using the free kit.

title: A copyright-safe family picture-book club for learning Zhuyin
body:
Families learning Traditional Chinese often need something between “read more books” and a scored worksheet. They also need a resource that does not quietly redistribute copyrighted picture books.

I built a **free bilingual four-week family Zhuyin picture-book club kit**:

- English: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/zhuyin-family-picture-book-club-kit.html
- 繁體中文: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/zh-Hant/tools/zhuyin-family-picture-book-club-kit.html

The family supplies a book it legally owns, borrows from a library or accesses through an authorized service. The page supplies only original before-during-after prompts and a blank, non-scored reading log. It never asks for a title, quote, scan or image; it hosts no book copies and links to no unauthorized copies.

Across four weeks, the child first chooses and notices, then joins one familiar word, leads a page, and finally retells with pictures or props. Listening, pointing, acting and drawing all count as participation. Ten minutes is a gentle structure—not a target to force.

The evidence statement is deliberately narrow. A 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis covered 19 randomized trials with 2,594 children. Book-sharing interventions had small average effects on expressive and receptive language and a larger effect on caregiver book-sharing competence: https://centaur.reading.ac.uk/80756/

That review did **not** test Zhuyin, this exact four-week or ten-minute schedule, independent reading or this tool. The kit says so instead of promising faster learning or better scores.

For unfamiliar characters, families can check Taiwan's official Ministry of Education Mini Dictionary: https://dict.mini.moe.edu.tw/. The original prompts and log are CC BY 4.0; that license does not apply to any picture book or external source. The page has no account, form submission, local storage, upload or saved child profile.

title: A privacy-first Zhuyin handoff between weekend school and home
body:
Weekend Chinese schools and families often have the same problem: the teacher knows exactly what was modeled in class, but the family receives either a broad worksheet or no usable cue for the days between classes.

I built a **free bilingual Zhuyin parent-teacher handoff kit** around a deliberately small loop:

- English: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/zhuyin-parent-teacher-handoff-kit.html
- 繁體中文: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/zh-Hant/tools/zhuyin-parent-teacher-handoff-kit.html

The teacher selects only one to three symbols, tones, blends or annotated words already taught. The family uses a ten-minute choose → model → move → use → celebrate routine. A paper return slip records whether the child listened, pointed, traced, joined a sound or asked to stop—never correct/incorrect and never a score.

The page asks for no child name, class, diagnosis, contact detail or online submission. It has no account, form, upload, local storage or saved profile. The printable slip also works without a name, so schools can apply their own offline privacy policy.

The evidence boundary is explicit. This original handoff template has not been evaluated in a trial, and it cannot diagnose a child, prove Zhuyin gains or promise that ten minutes improves learning. Taiwan Ministry of Education and OCAC links establish standard notation, stroke order and longer-form resources; they do not endorse this kit.

The original cards are CC BY 4.0, so heritage schools may print, adapt and translate them with attribution. Lumi Bopomofo appears only as an optional practice layer after the teacher chooses the weekly focus; the complete handoff works with paper and teacher modeling alone.

title: Designing a rights-aware Zhuyin storytime kit for libraries
body:
A library family program needs more than a list of Zhuyin activities. It needs a repeatable clock, participation choices, a clear privacy boundary—and an honest answer to the question of who has approved the book and each planned use.

I built a **free bilingual 30-minute Zhuyin library storytime kit**:

- English: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/zhuyin-library-storytime-kit.html
- 繁體中文: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/zh-Hant/tools/zhuyin-library-storytime-kit.html

The six phases move from welcome choices and three-symbol warm-up to meaning-first shared reading, a blank symbol hunt, open retelling and one gentle family prompt. Listening, pointing, joining, watching or stopping all count as participation. The printable kit also includes an optional aggregate facilitator note with no attendance names.

**The rights boundary is deliberately strict.** The page contains no story and grants no right to perform, display, record, stream, photograph, scan or distribute a book. Library staff must approve the selected title and every planned use under their current local law, licenses, publisher terms and policy. Recording and livestreaming are not treated as automatically permitted. The CC BY 4.0 license covers only the original routine and blank cards—not any book or external source.

The privacy boundary is equally explicit: no registration, child-name field, attendance form, account, camera, microphone, upload, local storage or saved child profile. The title used, paper notes, images, audio and video are never submitted to the page.

I also avoided turning broad research into a product claim. A 2020 systematic review and meta-analysis covered 19 randomized trials with 2,594 children and reported small average expressive- and receptive-language effects for parent/caregiver book-sharing interventions, plus a larger effect on caregiver book-sharing competence: https://centaur.reading.ac.uk/80756/

Those studies did not test group library storytime, Zhuyin, a 30-minute format, the symbol hunt or this kit. The page says so plainly and promises no language gain, reading score or attendance result.

The complete program works with an approved book, facilitator interaction and the original printable cards. Lumi Bopomofo appears only as optional take-home practice after the program, never as a requirement for running it.

title: Why I made a 14-day Zhuyin warm-up that does not measure readiness
body:
Search for summer Zhuyin practice and you can find many useful flashcards, tracing sheets and games. What is harder to find is a small day-by-day structure that an English-dominant or Traditional Chinese-speaking parent can print, start gently and stop without turning it into a score.

I built a **free bilingual 14-day Grade 1 Zhuyin summer warm-up calendar**:

- English: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/zhuyin-grade1-14-day-summer-calendar.html
- 繁體中文: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/zh-Hant/tools/zhuyin-grade1-14-day-summer-calendar.html

The first choice is not an age level. It is one of three flexible lanes for today:

1. Completely new: use only two or three symbols; adult modeling and listening are enough.
2. Recognises some: use four to six familiar symbols for pointing, matching and movement.
3. Ready to combine: use two familiar two-part blends without speed or handwriting pressure.

Every day follows the same eight-to-ten-minute ceiling: choose, model once, play, connect to paper or an authorized book, name one effort and stop. The activities rotate through listening, shape matching, official stroke reference, tone movement, simple blending and noticing Zhuyin during real reading. Day 7 repeats by child choice; Day 14 ends with a neutral next step rather than a level.

**The calendar deliberately refuses the usual readiness claim.** It does not teach or assess all 37 symbols, set an entrance requirement, assign a level or predict school performance. Taiwan Ministry of Education references establish standard symbol forms, notation and stroke order; they did not prescribe or endorse this independent sequence. The 14-day routine itself has not been evaluated in a study.

Official references:
- Bopomofo Handbook: https://language.moe.gov.tw/001/Upload/files/site_content/M0001/juyin/html_ch/index.html
- Zhuyin stroke order: https://stroke-order.learningweb.moe.edu.tw/phonetic.jsp?la=0

The privacy design is intentionally boring: no child name, date field, completion tracker, account, form submission, camera, microphone, upload, local storage or saved profile. Nothing is sent to the page.

The original calendar is CC BY 4.0. The complete routine works with paper, official references and a legally available annotated book. Lumi Bopomofo is only an optional listening, tracing, tone or blending activity inside a day, with an optional one-time lifetime unlock—not a requirement for using the calendar.

title: A private printable travel mission generator with no photo challenges
body:
Most printable airport and road-trip scavenger hunts begin with a fixed PDF. I wanted a reusable version that covers more of a family trip without asking a parent to enter a child's name, destination, route or itinerary.

I built a **free bilingual family travel mission-card generator**:

- English: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/tools/family-travel-mission-card-generator.html
- 繁體中文: https://alice51849.github.io/ios-app-guide/zh-Hant/tools/family-travel-mission-card-generator.html

It covers 12 settings: before leaving, airport, flight, road trip, train or ferry, city walk, museum, theme park, nature or beach, hotel, restaurant and quiet waiting. A family chooses one flexible participation style—watch or point, notice or describe, or plan or create—and receives five optional observation cards plus one blank adult-approved card.

Those styles are choices, not ages or ability levels. A child can switch, watch, point, describe, imagine or skip every card. There is no score, reward requirement or completion tracker, and the tool makes no claim about behaviour, mood, learning or travel quality.

**The safety boundary is intentionally conservative.** Every prompt is stationary and adult-led. Airport cards do not ask for photographs. Flight cards stop for safety briefings, instructions or turbulence. Road-trip cards are passenger-only; the driver never reads, answers or operates them while driving. Carrier, crew, driver, security, venue, staff and local instructions always override a card.

Official boundary references:
- TSA checkpoint photography: https://www.tsa.gov/travel/frequently-asked-questions/can-i-film-and-take-photos-security-checkpoint
- FAA child restraint guidance: https://www.faa.gov/travelers/fly_children/child_safety_seat_tips
- NHTSA child passenger safety: https://www.nhtsa.gov/vehicle-safety/car-seats-and-booster-seats
- U.S. DOT family air-travel tips: https://www.transportation.gov/resources/individuals/aviation-consumer-protection/tips-families-and-links-airline-webpages

The sources define boundaries; they do not endorse this independent tool. Families still need to check current rules for the exact country, carrier, vehicle and venue.

The page contains no name, age, room number, destination, location, route, photo, video, audio, itinerary, form, account, upload, saved profile, score or completion record. It sends no analytics request and keeps the generated set only in the currently open page. The original prompts and blank-card layout are available under CC BY 4.0.
